text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#PD-987654): node-disconnect -> host-5271 in us-west1 reported kubelet NotReady. Auto-page to eng-oncall. Metrics: node.kubelet.status{state=NotReady}=1, pod.eviction.failures increased. Links: https://pd.example/PD-987654 / console: https://console.redwood/hosts/host-5271

alice.nguyen: Acked. I'm on it. Putting my status in the incident channel.

ben.kramer: seeing `NotReady` on the node: `kubectl get nodes host-5271 -o wide` returns `STATUS=NotReady` and last heartbeat 2m ago.

diana.ho: telemetry shows spike in inference 5xx for Dedicated pool r-west-3 since ~3232104380. Customer impact: Customers CUST-42 and CUST-77 showing increased request latencies, some timeouts.

sara.veld: trying to list pods: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=host-5271` -> several model-* pods in CrashLoopBackOff and some with `FailedAttachVolume`.

ben.kramer: attempt to cordon: `kubectl cordon host-5271` succeeded. drain failing with:
```
$ kubectl drain host-5271 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
error: eviction API version of the kubelet is not supported: unable to evict pod "model-worker-abc" from host-5271: pods with local storage found
```

infra-oncall: if drain fails because of volume attachments, we can force delete the pods after re-routing traffic. Recommend marking node unschedulable (cordon done) and failover traffic to fallback pool first.

josh.leung: attaching serial console now, grabbing dmesg and journal. Past few lines look like repeated NVMe controller errors and `nvme 2:0: controller reset failed` then `kubelet: node status lost`.

josh.leung: pasted tail of serial: 
```
[ 1234.567890] nvme 2:0: controller reset failed, retries=3
[ 1234.568012] nvme 2:0: aborting command, status=0x2
[ 1234.568123] gpu0: PCIe link error, AER: detected fatal error
[ 1234.568456] kernel: nvlink: resetting link, failed
[ 1234.570000] systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
```

diana.ho: pushing emergency routing: I'll flip dedicated-r-west alias to dedicated-fallback-1. Notifying product that customers are being routed. Expect ~30s for in-flight drains to complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alice.nguyen: go ahead diana, confirm when route switch is done and we can start force-evict strategy.

incident-bot: PD#PD-987654 status changed: acknowledged by alice.nguyen.

diana.ho: route switch done. Console link: https://console.redwood/routes/dedicated-r-west -> dedicated-fallback-1. Observability: latency dropping for CUST-42, error rate reduced in 60s.

ben.kramer: proceeding to force-evict remaining pods to free node resources so we can repro and collect artifacts. Using: `kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force` after capturing pod logs.

sara.veld: saved logs for model-worker-* to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-987654/host-5271/

infra-oncall: created internal incident ticket INC-2026-042 for host-5271 hardware investigation and possible RMA. Tagged hw-eng.

hw-eng: received INC-2026-042. From serial logs it looks like NVMe controller and PCIe errors; possible board-level issue or transient AER that persists. We'll run a remote power-cycle and re-flash NVMe firmware if remote cycle doesn't clear. ETA for on-site is 5h if RMA needed.

josh.leung: reboots attempted: `ipmi chassis power cycle` from hostpool succeeded. Node came back to network, but kubelet status cycles to Ready for ~40s then back to NotReady with same kernel message in serial.

alice.nguyen: summarizing for handoff -> Ben (next oncall).
- PD: PD-987654 (acked)
- Node: host-5271 (cordoned, drained partially, pods force-evicted)
- Impact: two dedicated customers saw increased 5xx/latency; traffic routed to dedicated-fallback-1, mitigation in place
- Artifacts: serial logs uploaded, pod logs in S3 (s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-987654/host-5271/), diagnostic bundle at https://console.redwood/diag/PD-987654
- Next steps: hw-eng to attempt remote power-cycle + firmware reflash; if persists schedule RMA. Keep PD incident open until node is stable or replaced.

ben.kramer: taking over. Will monitor hw-eng actions and keep customers updated. Setting my status to on-call-handoff. :thumbsup:

diana.ho: posted a short note to affected customers via support channel with mitigation steps and that we are routing traffic to fallback. Ticket refs: SUP-9981, SUP-9982.

incident-bot: PD#PD-987654 note added: "Handoff to Ben K. mitigation: traffic routed to fallback; HW investigation opened."

alice.nguyen: logging out of the incident for now. If HW can't clear with remote actions, we plan RMA and will coordinate time windows with customers.

hw-eng: performed remote power-cycle and NVMe firmware re-flash at 3232104780. Monitoring node now.

josh.leung: after firmware flash node stayed Ready for ~7m then kernel oops reappeared. Looks like an intermittent hardware fault.

ben.kramer: will keep PD open and continue monitoring. If node doesn't remain stable for 1h, schedule RMA. Closing on-call handoff notes here.

incident-bot: Page closed (auto) due to acknowledgement and handoff. PD#PD-987654 remains open until hardware resolution.

alice.nguyen: final note: docs updated at https://wiki.redwood/incidents/PD-987654 with timeline and mitigation runbook additions (add forced-evict checklist and fallback-route playbook). Thanks team. :heart:
